name: Stamps Scholarship
value: Full-ride package covering cost of attendance, plus $16,000 in enrichment funds over four years for study abroad, research, internships, conferences and leadership training.
deadline: Fall 2027 dates not yet posted. The fall 2026 cycle required the UA admission application by December 1, 2025 and the Stamps application by January 21, 2026.
apply: Invitation-only separate Stamps application for eligible UA applicants, with a short essay up to 500 words and activities resume; semifinalist and finalist interview stages follow.
eligibility: As listed for the fall 2026 cycle: Arizona resident and US citizen, unweighted GPA of 3.75 or higher, incoming first-time University of Arizona student.
notes: The official page still describes the fall 2026 entry cycle. Confirm eligibility and dates for fall 2027 when the page is updated.

name: Stamps Scholarship
value: Covers the full educational costs of a bachelor's degree, plus up to $10,000 in enrichment funds for research, conferences, study abroad and unpaid internships or co-ops.
deadline: Apply to Purdue West Lafayette and complete the John Martinson Honors College portion of the application by November 1 (displayed without a year).
apply: No open application. Purdue does a preliminary holistic review of admission applications and invites a select number of students to apply for its prestigious merit awards, including Stamps.
eligibility: US citizens or permanent residents entering Purdue West Lafayette as first-year students who complete the Honors College portion of the application by the deadline.

name: Stamps Scholarship
value: Full cost-of-attendance scholarship renewable for four years (eight semesters), plus $12,000 for research and experiential learning. Storrs campus only.
deadline: Common App or Coalition Application by November 1, 2026. Stamps Scholarship Supplemental Application and all required documents by November 8, 2026.
apply: Supplemental application in the UConn applicant portal: three short answers of 100, 200 and 100 words, detailed resume and two recommendation letters. Selected applicants interview with UConn and Stamps. Early Decision Stamps results come in early February.
eligibility: Students graduating secondary school and entering UConn Storrs in Fall 2027, with leadership and community service. Expected GPA 3.8 on a 4.0 scale and top 10% rank if available; test optional, with expected 1420 SAT or 32 ACT if submitted. Apply to only one of Stamps, Nutmeg or Day of Pride.

name: Stamps and Lombardi Scholarships (Preeminent Scholars Program)
value: Stamps Scholars: funding valued up to the full cost of attendance for up to four years, plus $10,000 in experiential funding. Lombardi Scholars: annual stipend of $7,000 for up to four years. Both receive four fully funded summer enrichment experiences.
deadline: Fall 2027 dates not yet posted. In the last cycle the application link was emailed to Honors admits one week after January 2026 admission decisions, and finalist interviews were held March 7, 2026.
apply: Apply to UF by Early Action and to the Honors Program. Admitted Honors students receive an emailed scholarship application. Finalists attend a mandatory in-person interview on campus. High school nomination and recommendation letters are no longer required.
eligibility: Students admitted to UF and the Honors Program via Early Action. Non-Florida residents and international students may apply. Transfer students are not eligible.
notes: About 10 Stamps and 10 Lombardi Scholars per class. Official pages still show fall 2026 cycle dates.

name: Stamps Scholarship
value: Funding valued up to the full estimated cost of attendance for up to four years, including an out-of-state tuition waiver for non-Florida residents, plus $20,000 in enrichment funding and participation in the Presidential Scholars Program.
deadline: Apply to FSU and submit the University Honors Program/Presidential Scholars essay by 11:59 p.m. EST on December 1, 2026. Semifinalist video responses due February 28, 2027. Finalist Recruitment Weekend is April 2 to 3, 2027.
apply: Stamps selection is part of the Presidential Scholars Program process: answer Yes to the Honors Program question on the FSU application and submit the Honors essay. Semifinalists submit two video responses, finalists interview on campus, and Presidential Scholars nominated for Stamps interview with the national Stamps Scholars Program.
eligibility: High school seniors admitted to the FSU Honors Program and selected as Presidential Scholars. Five Stamps Scholars are named each year.
notes: Renewal requires 15 credits per semester, cumulative FSU GPA at least 3.0 and successful degree progress.

name: Presidential Scholars Program
value: $42,000 over four years, plus an out-of-state tuition waiver for nonresidents. Official pages give conflicting waiver estimates of $73,808 and $73,080.
deadline: Apply to FSU and submit the University Honors Program/Presidential Scholars essay by 11:59 p.m. EST on December 1, 2026. Semifinalist video responses due February 28, 2027. Finalist Recruitment Weekend is April 2 to 3, 2027.
apply: Students who apply to the University Honors Program are automatically considered for this invitation-only program. Semifinalists submit two video responses and finalists attend a required on-campus interview during Recruitment Weekend.
eligibility: High school seniors admitted to the Florida State University Honors Program.
notes: Renewal requires 15 credits per semester, cumulative FSU GPA at least 3.0 and successful degree progress. Five Presidential Scholars are also Stamps Scholars.

name: Stamps Scholarship
value: Covers full cost of attendance, plus up to $12,000 in enrichment funds.
deadline: No separate scholarship application or scholarship deadline is listed. Candidates are identified from Illinois admission applications.
apply: No scholarship application. Illinois admission applications are reviewed to identify candidates, who are invited in early spring for a campus visit that includes an interview with a selection committee.
eligibility: Only Illinois residents are reviewed for the Stamps Scholarship.
notes: Renewal requires a 3.0 GPA, full-time enrollment and program engagement, for up to 8 consecutive fall and spring semesters.

name: Stamps Scholarship
value: Four-year, full cost of attendance scholarship, plus a $16,000 enrichment fund. Scholars must stay in the Honors College all four years.
deadline: Premier Scholars application and recommendation letters due Dec. 1 (displayed without a year). Applying to Mizzou and the Honors College by Nov. 1 is strongly encouraged.
apply: Apply to Mizzou and the Honors College, then submit the Premier Scholars application: a 500 to 750 word essay and two recommendation letters (one from a teacher or counselor). About 100 quarterfinalists submit a video interview; about 20 semifinalists attend a required in-person interview weekend at their own travel cost.
eligibility: Students in an accredited U.S. or international high school with ACT at least 32 or SAT 1420 and core GPA at least 3.5, admitted to Mizzou and Honors before the deadline. International applicants abroad are not currently considered; those lawfully in the U.S. as permanent residents, asylum seekers, refugees or on a nonimmigrant visa may apply.
notes: Interview weekend dates shown on the page (Feb. 5 to 7, 2026) are from the prior cycle; confirm fall 2027 dates. The same application covers the Brazeal, Boomba Tiger and Discovery Fellows awards.

name: Stamps Scholarship
value: Oregon residents: full UO tuition, fees, food and housing for four years. Out-of-state recipients: nonresident tuition and fees. All scholars: up to $12,000 in enrichment funds. About $125,000 (residents) or $185,000 (nonresidents) over four years.
deadline: Fall 2027 dates not yet posted. For the 2026-2027 award: apply Early Action by November 1 and submit the Stamps application and admission materials by November 15.
apply: Separate Stamps Scholarship Application in the UO Scholarship Dashboard with four short-answer essays. Semifinalists interview on campus; finalists are interviewed by the Stamps Scholars Program.
eligibility: Incoming domestic first-year students with a minimum 3.85 cumulative high school GPA on a 4.00 scale.
notes: About 20 awards annually. Cannot combine with most UO scholarships. Renewal requires 3.25 UO GPA and 12 UO credits per term, for up to 12 undergraduate terms over five years. The page still describes 2026-2027.

name: Stamps Scholarship
value: Funding for four years for estimated cost of attendance, including tuition, fees, room and board, plus an enrichment fund for experiential learning.
deadline: Virginia Tech Early Action deadline, November 15 (displayed without a year). Students applying after Early Action cannot be considered.
apply: All Early Action applicants are considered using their VT and Common App materials. The page also says applicants who indicate Honors College interest complete a Stamps application on VT Scholarship Central by the posted deadline. Semifinalists are contacted in mid-January and finalists are interviewed in February.
eligibility: First-year applicants to Virginia Tech who apply Early Action and indicate interest in the Honors College.
notes: The page describes both automatic consideration and a Scholarship Central application. Check Scholarship Central after applying.

name: 1693 Scholars Program
value: Benefits worth the amount of in-state tuition, general fees, housing and dining, plus $5,000 to support independent projects and faculty mentoring. About eight entering students per year.
deadline: No separate application. The latest posted timeline (2026) used the January 5 first-year application deadline; the fall 2027 timeline has not been posted.
apply: All first-year applicants are reviewed. About 200 semifinalists submit one essay (200 to 300 words) and a short video (3 minutes maximum). Finalists complete a virtual interview with alumni and a virtual presentation to faculty, and about 15 attend an on-campus weekend.
eligibility: All first-year applicants, including Early Decision, Early Decision II, Regular Decision, St Andrews joint degree and international applicants.
notes: Finalists typically rank in the top 5% and score above 1500 SAT or 33 ACT; these are typical profiles, not minimums. W&M is test-optional. Some 1693 Scholars are named Stamps 1693 Scholars.

name: Stamps and Presidential Scholarships
value: Both cover tuition, fees, on-campus housing and a seven-day meal plan. Stamps adds $4,000 annual living stipend and $10,000 one-time enrichment; Presidential adds $2,000 annual living stipend and $5,000 one-time study-abroad stipend.
deadline: Scholarship application by 11:59 p.m. EST on November 15, 2026. Complete GSU application by the November 15, 2026 priority deadline. Recommendation letter by November 20, 2026.
apply: Separate Stamps and Presidential Scholarship application with one letter of recommendation. Finalists attend Scholarship Day interviews in spring 2027; international students may interview virtually.
eligibility: Incoming first-year students planning to attend the Atlanta campus in fall 2027 and pursuing a first bachelor's degree. Stamps requires living in Georgia and eligibility for HOPE or Zell Miller. Out-of-state and international students are eligible only for the Presidential Scholarship. No minimum GPA, but applicants must qualify for the Honors College. SAT and ACT scores are not considered.
notes: Stamps requires Georgia residence and HOPE/Zell Miller eligibility; Presidential permits out-of-state and international students. Renewal requires 3.5 GPA, at least 12 credits and program participation.

name: Stamps Scholarship
value: Full tuition and fees, housing and food, an Apple iPad, and up to $16,000 enrichment stipend over four years.
deadline: Application for admission and all supporting documents by November 1 (displayed without a year).
apply: No separate scholarship application is listed. Eligible accepted students are invited to Presidential Scholars Weekend to interview with faculty, staff and alumni; select candidates advance to further committee interviews.
eligibility: Incoming first-year students who submit the admission application and all documents by November 1 and demonstrate leadership, perseverance, scholarship, service and innovation. Ten scholars are selected each year.

name: Stamps Scholars Program
value: Annual renewable scholarship for tuition, books, room and board, and transportation, plus an additional $6,000 award for study abroad or another learning experience.
deadline: December 15 at 11:59 PM EST (displayed without a year). The application season opens September 15.
apply: Accepted students who meet the GPA minimum apply through MyBarry with a letter of recommendation, a resume and a personal video (3 minutes maximum). Semifinalists have a virtual interview in early February; finalists interview with a Stamps Scholars Program representative in March.
eligibility: First-year students (US citizen, resident or international) with a high school GPA of 3.5 or higher and demonstrated, active leadership.
notes: Annual renewal depends on GPA, leadership training and community service.

name: Stamps Scholarship
value: Scholarship equal to 100% of annual tuition, renewable for up to eight semesters, plus $6,000 in enrichment funds and automatic admission to the Honors Program.
deadline: January 15 (displayed without a year): complete application and all required documents.
apply: No separate application. About 25 semifinalists are invited to interviews in February, and about 10 to 15 finalists interview with the national Stamps Scholars Program. Test scores and an Honors interview are strongly recommended but not required, and optional essays are strongly encouraged.
eligibility: Open to US citizens, US permanent residents and international students who submit a complete application by January 15.

name: Stamps Scholarship
value: Four-year, full-ride scholarship covering the entire cost of attending Morehouse, worth up to $230,000 per student, with access to an enrichment fund (per the October 2024 announcement).
deadline: Not published.
apply: Not published. The official announcement does not describe how scholars are selected.
eligibility: Incoming Morehouse first-year students. At least five scholars per year were planned starting in 2025. Morehouse is a men's college.
notes: A September 2026 official release confirms ongoing Stamps support. Current selection process and application terms are not published.

name: Stamps Scholarship
value: Covers total cost of attendance (tuition, mandatory fees, housing and meals), plus an enrichment fund for study abroad, research, conferences and unpaid internships. About 10 awarded each year.
deadline: Semifinalists are invited to submit supplements by January 5th (displayed without a year).
apply: No open application. Semifinalists are invited to submit supplements, and finalists are invited to interview in the spring.
eligibility: First-year applicants to Tulane.
notes: Tulane expects CSS Profile and FAFSA from eligible domestic applicants and financial declarations from international applicants; scores are optional but preferred for academic merit.

name: Grossman & Cohen Scholarship
value: Covers tuition, mandatory fees, housing and meals, renewable for up to eight semesters, with an expected total value of roughly $400,000.
deadline: No separate application or scholarship deadline is listed.
apply: No additional application. Recipients are selected on academic record, standardized test scores and impact outside the classroom. Finalists may be invited to interview with admission committee members in late winter or early spring.
eligibility: Awarded to Tulane's very top first-year candidates.
notes: Tulane asks all scholarship candidates to complete the CSS Profile and FAFSA (international students: the Declaration and Certification of Finances) for consideration for merit up to full tuition.

name: Stamps, Carolina and 1801 Scholars Awards (S.C. residents)
value: Stamps Scholars: $20,000 per year ($80,000 over four years) plus a $15,000 enrichment fund. Carolina Scholars: $15,000 per year ($60,000) plus a $15,000 enrichment fund. 1801 Scholars: $10,000 per year ($40,000).
deadline: Honors application November 15; required credentials and recommendation December 1. Mandatory finalist weekend February 27-March 1, 2027.
apply: Apply for university admission and Honors with two additional essays, one recommendation and unofficial transcript; optional resume and scores. Semifinalists interview virtually in late January; finalists attend the mandatory Top Scholar Weekend.
eligibility: South Carolina residents. Fifty awards per year: 5 Stamps, 20 Carolina and up to 25 1801 Scholars.
notes: Published averages (1530 SAT, 5.3 GPA, top 1% of class) describe last year's scholars and are not minimums. Nonresidents are considered for the separate McNair Scholars program.

name: Haslam Leadership Scholars
value: Endowed scholarship covering tuition, mandatory fees and on-campus housing, a fully funded faculty-led cohort study abroad experience after the first year, and professional development funding for research, conferences, creative ventures or internships.
deadline: UT Early Action application by November 1, 2026. UT application complete by November 15, 2026. Haslam Leadership Scholars application by 11:59 p.m. ET on November 20, 2026.
apply: Apply to UT Early Action, then complete invited Honors/Haslam application with a video under five minutes recorded directly in Go Vols Portal. Semifinalists interview by Zoom; finalists attend spring selection weekend.
eligibility: Incoming first-year students who apply to UT by Early Action and receive the emailed invitation to apply for University Honors. About 15 scholars per year.
notes: The fall 2026 cohort had 15 Tennessee residents and 1 out-of-state student; residency is not stated as a requirement.

name: Honors College Fellowships (Honors College, Bodenhamer, Sturgis)
value: Up to $80,000 ($20,000 per year). Can be combined with Arkansas state scholarships (in-state) or the New Arkansan Non-Resident Tuition Award (out-of-state). About 70 to 80 Honors College Fellowships and 5 to 6 each of the Bodenhamer and Sturgis Fellowships per year.
deadline: Nov. 15 priority scholarship deadline (apply to the university by Nov. 1) or Feb. 1 final deadline (apply by Jan. 15). Dates displayed without a year. Recommendation letters are due by the final deadline.
apply: University application, fellowship application with essay up to 600 words, activities, awards and two recommendations; Honors application is also required. Finalists interview in March.
eligibility: Incoming first-year students with 32 ACT composite from one exam or 1430 SAT and 3.90 weighted high-school GPA, recalculated on a 4.0 scale with AP/IB/dual-enrollment weighting only. Honors/Bodenhamer permit all majors; Sturgis requires Fulbright College, service and intellectual curiosity.
notes: Fellows must join Honors and ordinarily live in Hotz Honors Hall first year; the award replaces other U of A academic scholarships but can combine with state aid or nonresident tuition awards.

name: Cutler Scholars Program
value: Many awards are $25,000 annual renewable scholarships. Russ Legacy, McClain High School and Olean High School awards are described as full scholarships; the Stuckey award amount is not listed.
deadline: Submit the Common Application by the November 15 Early Action deadline (displayed without a year) to receive the supplemental application.
apply: Eligible students who meet the Early Action deadline are sent a supplemental application. Finalists are invited to virtual interviews, typically late January and early February, and are notified by late March.
eligibility: Freshman applicants who attend a benefactor-designated high school (geographic awards) or apply to an eligible college or major (discipline awards). Discipline awards are for Ohio residents, except the Russ Legacy Award, which is open to in-state and out-of-state students. Test scores are not considered.
notes: This is a collection of awards restricted to specified high schools or fields. Consult the Fall 2027 list for each award.

name: Johnson Scholars Program
value: Merit scholarship covering full tuition, renewable for up to four years, plus eligibility for up to $10,000 in professional development funds after the first year. The university also commits to meeting each scholar's full demonstrated need.
deadline: Must be admitted in the Early Action or Early Decision I round and apply to the University Honors Program. Dates are not listed on the program page; finalists attend a virtual Selection Day in mid-March.
apply: Admitted EA and ED I applicants may apply to the University Honors Program. Johnson finalists are chosen from that pool and attend a virtual Selection Day; 5 scholars are selected.
eligibility: Early Action and Early Decision I admits to Santa Clara. International students are not eligible.
notes: Scholars must maintain a 3.5 GPA, take part in the honors program and file the FAFSA each year.

name: Honors Program scholarships (including Kenan Honors Fellow)
value: $15,000 annual Honors scholarship plus a $12,000 Presidential Scholarship ($27,000 per year, $108,000 over four years), a $1,000 Global Study grant and a $1,000 thesis research grant. One Honors student each year is named the William R. Kenan, Jr. Honors Fellow with a full tuition scholarship.
deadline: Honors Program application by November 10 (displayed without a year).
apply: Separate Honors Program application. Selection is based on high school record, essays, teacher recommendations and a faculty interview. Sixty students are selected each year.
eligibility: Students with a demanding high school curriculum, an excellent GPA and a top class rank.
notes: Elon admission is test optional. Scholarship renewal requires academic performance and participation in Honors.

name: Marquis Fellowship and Marquis Scholarship
value: Marquis Fellowship: full tuition. Marquis Scholarship: half tuition. Both are tied to tuition and grow with annual increases, renewable for up to eight semesters with a 3.00 GPA.
deadline: Admission application deadline January 5 (displayed without a year). Applying a few weeks earlier is strongly encouraged for merit consideration.
apply: No additional application. All first-time Early Decision and Regular Decision applicants are considered, and awards appear in the admission letter. An admissions interview is encouraged.
eligibility: First-time applicants to Lafayette. Offers typically go to students at the top of their class in the most demanding curriculum.
notes: Lafayette also offers Cur Non Scholarships of $17,500 to $31,500. Students whose enrollment depends on merit aid are advised to apply Regular Decision.

name: Macaulay Tuition and Merit Scholarship Package
value: Tuition scholarship covering 8 semesters of full-time undergraduate tuition for students meeting CUNY's New York State residency requirements. It pays tuition remaining after other aid and scholarships; fees are excluded. Includes the NYC Cultural Passport and access to the Opportunities Fund.
deadline: Early Decision (binding): October 26, 2026 at 6 PM, including transcripts, essays and supporting materials. Regular: November 16, 2026 at 6 PM; regular recommendations due November 30 at 11:59 PM. Time zone is not specified.
apply: Separate Macaulay application through the CUNY application, not the Fast App, with two essays of about 500 words each, official transcripts, two academic recommendations and a $65 fee (waivers may be available). Choose one Macaulay home campus.
eligibility: First-time college students (incoming freshmen). The tuition scholarship requires meeting CUNY's New York State residency requirements for in-state tuition.
notes: Students must file the FAFSA and TAP application (or the NYS DREAM Act application) each year to keep the tuition scholarship. CUNY is test-optional.

name: Presidential Scholarship
value: Full tuition (excluding summers) for five years or until an undergraduate degree is earned.
deadline: February 1 (displayed without a year) for the admission application, transcript, official test score and Presidential Scholarship application.
apply: Apply for admission and the Presidential Scholarship with a one-page resume and short answers; submit official transcripts and required test scores and complete an official campus visit by February 1. A 45-second video and meeting with an admission counselor are strongly suggested.
eligibility: First-year applicants need ACT superscore 28 or SAT 1300, plus one of: College Board Recognition Program scholar in the top 10% of class, top 5% of class, or weighted GPA 4.0 on a 4.0 scale. Schools reporting only unweighted GPA receive individual consideration. Transfer applicants have a separate route requiring a 3.7 college GPA and, for fewer than 30 college credits, qualifying test scores.
notes: A campus visit is required. Recipients must take 15 credit hours per semester. Information session dates on the page are from fall 2025.

name: Foundation Scholarship
value: Covers financial aid cost of attendance for up to eight undergraduate semesters or completion of a bachelor's degree, whichever comes first, plus a one-time $4,500 study abroad or academic enhancement stipend. Reduced by any Promise Scholarship; multiple majors receive the tuition cost of the most expensive major only.
deadline: Must be admitted to WVU as a first-time freshman by January 19, 2027.
apply: Eligible students receive application materials by mail, usually starting in late October or early November. Five recipients are chosen by a selection committee from the pool of 20 Bucklew Scholars.
eligibility: West Virginia residents graduating from a West Virginia high school, or home-schooled in West Virginia for at least senior year, with at least a 3.80 high school GPA and ACT 30 or SAT 1360. Must be admitted as a degree-seeking first-time freshman by January 19, 2027. Online programs are ineligible.
notes: Renewal requires at least a 2.75 overall GPA, 30 earned credits per academic year and full-time enrollment of at least 12 credits per semester.

name: Society of Yeager Scholars
value: Four-year full scholarship: full tuition and fees, room and board, a textbook stipend, a personal computer, and support for study abroad or, with permission, an approved internship or research. The curriculum includes study abroad at the University of Oxford.
deadline: December 15, 2026, including recommendation letters.
apply: Apply to Marshall first, then submit the Top Scholar application (one application for all Honors College scholarships) with two letters of reference, one academic.
eligibility: First-time, first-year students entering in fall 2027 with at least a 3.5 unweighted cumulative high school GPA; ACT 30 or SAT 1360 from a single test date is recommended. Dual enrollment is allowed. Recipients cannot enroll in an accelerated undergraduate program.
notes: Renewal requires a 3.5 GPA, documented service and leadership, and appropriate conduct. December test scores are accepted for the December 15, 2026 deadline.

name: Buchanan Fellowship
value: Full tuition waiver (up to 16 credit hours per semester for four years), a $500 per semester book allowance, up to $5,000 for approved study abroad, plus priority registration and special seminars.
deadline: For fall 2027: early review November 1, 2026 or regular review December 1, 2026, by 11:59 PM Central Standard Time. All transcripts and test scores are due by the chosen deadline. Early review requires accepting the fellowship if selected.
apply: Apply to MTSU, create a PipelineMT account, then complete the Buchanan Fellowship application. Send high school and any dual enrollment transcripts to Admissions and the Honors College through the permitted upload, counselor portal or mail routes; Honors does not accept emailed transcripts. Resume is optional; recommendation letters are not considered.
eligibility: Minimum ACT of 30 or SAT of 1360 and a minimum unweighted GPA of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale. Limited to 20 students per year.
notes: Choosing early review requires committing to MTSU in December if offered the fellowship. Fellows must maintain a cumulative 3.25 GPA and complete Buchanan courses, Honors requirements and a thesis.

name: STRIDE Scholarship
value: $22,500 per year for four years, plus a $3,000 annual research assistant stipend for the first two years. Total four-year award $96,000.
deadline: No separate application or deadline; scholars are selected at the time of admission.
apply: Selected at admission based on outstanding academic and personal potential. About 50 awarded per year.
eligibility: Incoming first-year Smith students.
notes: Renewal requires satisfactory academic progress. Merit scholarships count toward calculated financial need and may reduce need-based grants.

name: Dora Windes Zollman Scholarship
value: Half of the tuition cost for four years. Zollman Scholars are also invited to join the STRIDE paid research program.
deadline: No separate application or deadline; awarded at the time of admission.
apply: Selected at admission. Awarded to fewer than ten first-year students based on exceptional promise.
eligibility: U.S. citizens entering Smith as first-year students.
notes: Renewal requires satisfactory academic progress. Merit scholarships count toward calculated financial need and may reduce need-based grants.

name: Day of Pride Scholarship
value: Full scholarship including direct and indirect cost of attendance (some restrictions may apply). Storrs campus.
deadline: Common App or Coalition Application by November 1, 2026. Day of Pride Supplemental Application and all required documents by November 8, 2026.
apply: Apply for admission by November 1, then submit the Day of Pride supplement by November 8 with short responses of 100, 200 and 100 words, a detailed resume and two recommendations. Interviews may be required. Choose only one of Day of Pride, Nutmeg or Stamps.
eligibility: Connecticut residents graduating from a Connecticut secondary school and enrolling at Storrs in fall 2027. Applicants must be a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or undocumented student resident in Connecticut for at least two years, with at least a 3.6 GPA on a 4.0 scale and top 15% class rank if available. Leadership, community contributions and documented financial need are considered. Optional submitted scores should be SAT 1170 or ACT 24. Up to 20 recipients.
notes: UConn lists documented financial need as an eligibility factor.

name: Out-of-state and international automatic merit scholarships
value: Fall 2027 table, per year, GPA 3.50+ unless noted: Crimson Legends 25-26 ACT or 1200-1250 SAT $6,000; Capstone 27 ACT or 1260-1290 SAT $8,000; Collegiate 28 ACT or 1300-1320 SAT $10,000; Foundation in Excellence 29 ACT or 1330-1350 SAT $15,000; UA Scholar 30-31 ACT or 1360-1410 SAT $24,000; Presidential 32-36 ACT or 1420-1600 SAT $28,000; Presidential Elite 36 ACT or 1600 SAT with 4.0+ GPA: value of tuition for up to four years plus first-year housing, $1,500 per year and a $2,000 one-time allowance.
deadline: Summer/Fall 2027: application and official score reports due by December 4 (priority deadline). Later applicants considered as funds allow.
apply: Automatic with the UA undergraduate application. Send official ACT or SAT scores from the testing agency by December 4.
eligibility: Out-of-state and international first-time freshmen (same names and values). GPA considered through end of junior year. A test score is required for automatic awards; composite or total from a single test date (no superscores).
notes: Renewal requires a cumulative 3.0 UA GPA and completion of at least 67% of attempted UA credits, reviewed each semester. Students without test scores cannot receive automatic awards but may qualify for competitive scholarships. Separate from Academic Elite.

name: Non-resident Academic Merit Scholarships
deadline: No application deadline listed; qualifying tests must be taken before enrolling as a new freshman.
apply: Automatic with admission to the University of Mississippi.
eligibility: Entering nonresident freshmen with at least a 3.0 high school GPA and no more than 18 college credits earned after high school, excluding dual enrollment. Test-optional awards are available; ACT/SAT superscores must use scores from the same exam type.
notes: The official page publishes the 2026-2027 table; fall 2027 amounts are not posted. Awards pay toward nonresident fees and cannot stack with Academic Success NR or the National Merit package. Renewal is conditional on the award's terms for up to four years.

name: Freshman Non-Resident Academic Scholarship
value: Fall 2027 (2027-2028) per year, based on 9th-11th grade GPA: 3.30-3.59 $12,000 ($48,000 over four years); 3.60-4.09 $16,000 ($64,000); 4.10+ $19,000 ($76,000). Also automatic Freshman One-Year Housing Scholarship (double room, first year only) for 34+ ACT or 1490+ SAT with 3.00+ GPA.
deadline: Automatic upon admission; no deadline stated for this award. Housing scholarship uses ACT/SAT tests through the February test date of senior year.
apply: Automatic upon admission to MSU (Starkville). No separate application.
eligibility: Out-of-state and international first-time freshmen entering in 2027-2028 and assessed nonresident tuition. Uses the higher of the six-semester transcript GPA or MSU-calculated core GPA. No test score is required for the tuition award. The tuition award starts at 3.3 GPA; the separately listed one-year housing award starts at 3.0 GPA with ACT 34 or SAT 1490.
notes: Cannot be combined with the National Merit packages or the Presidential Endowed Scholarship Package, or with non-resident waivers such as Academic Common Market. Renewal: 3.0 college GPA and 12 hours each semester.

name: New Arkansan Non-Resident Tuition Award (NRTA)
value: 2026-2027 terms. Students from GA, IL, KS, LA, MS, MO, OK, TN, TX: 3.80+ GPA pays 90% of the difference between in-state and out-of-state tuition; 3.60+ pays 80%; 3.20+ pays 70%. Students from all other states (Extended States NRTA): 3.60+ pays 80%; 3.20+ pays 50%. Guide lists annual values of $15,600-$20,000 (listed states) and $11,100-$17,800 (other states) based on 30 hours.
deadline: NRTA has no separate application deadline. Qualifying GPA must be earned before the first day of classes. Additional competitive merit awards require their own scholarship application, with February 1 listed as the final deadline without a cycle year.
apply: Automatic with admission. No scholarship application required for the NRTA.
eligibility: Admitted non-resident freshmen with a 3.20+ cumulative high school GPA on a 4.0 scale (weighted credit given for AP, IB and concurrent courses).
notes: The published NRTA terms are effective for 2026-2027. Renewal requires 24 earned credits per academic year and a cumulative 2.75 GPA, for four years (five for architecture). Students with at least 24 transferable credits before finishing high school may request review under the transfer criteria.

name: Non-resident freshman merit scholarships
value: Fall 2026 table, four-year totals: Award of Excellence 31 ACT or 1390 SAT and 3.5 GPA $68,000 ($17,000 per year); Distinguished Scholar 29-30 ACT or 1330-1380 SAT and 3.5 $60,000 ($15,000); University Scholarship 28 ACT or 1300-1320 SAT and 3.5 $52,000 ($13,000); Academic Achievement 26-27 ACT or 1230-1290 SAT and 3.5 $48,000 ($12,000); Honor Award 26+ ACT or 1230+ SAT and 3.25-3.49 $44,000 ($11,000); Merit Award 24-25 ACT or 1160-1220 SAT and 3.5 $40,000 ($10,000). Test-optional non-residents: $24,000-$48,000 ($6,000-$12,000 per year) by holistic review.

notes: Page shows the fall 2026 table; fall 2027 not yet posted. Awards do not stack with each other.

name: Out-of-state freshman merit scholarships
value: By GPA on a 4.0 scale, four-year totals: KU Excellence 3.95+ $64,000 ($16,000 per year); KU Distinction 3.85-3.94 $56,000 ($14,000); KU Achievement 3.70-3.84 $48,000 ($12,000); KU Performance 3.5-3.69 $40,000 ($10,000); KU Access 3.25-3.49 $32,000 ($8,000).

apply: Automatic with a complete admission application by December 1. No test score needed.
eligibility: Out-of-state domestic freshmen enrolling in at least 12 credits each fall and spring immediately after high school. KU uses the sixth-semester weighted or unweighted GPA on a 4.0 scale, whichever benefits the student; weighted GPA must be school-wide and on the transcript. Exclusively online degrees are ineligible.
notes: Amounts are reviewed annually and the page does not specify an entering class. No seventh-semester upgrades or GPA rounding. Renewal requires a 3.0 KU GPA and full-time enrollment for the first bachelor's degree or eight continuous semesters, whichever comes first. Awards cannot stack with Missouri Tuition Reciprocity for architecture.

name: Out-of-state Academic Achievement Award plus state award
value: Fall 2027 per year: Academic Achievement Award 4.00+ $12,000; 3.90-3.99 $11,000; 3.80-3.89 $10,000; 3.70-3.79 $9,000; 3.60-3.69 $8,000; 3.50-3.59 $7,000; 3.40-3.49 $6,000; 3.30-3.39 $5,000; 3.20-3.29 $4,000; 3.10-3.19 $3,000. Added state award (3.00+): Excursion $5,000 (CA, TX); Exploration $3,000 (AZ, AR, CO, FL, GA, IN, MD, MI, NV, NJ, NY, OH, OK, PA, PR, TN, VA, WA); Expedition $2,000 (IL, KS, MO, NE, WI). eligibility: Out-of-state first-year students entering fall 2027 who are U.S. citizens, permanent residents, refugees or asylees. Generally must enroll immediately after high school; post-graduation college coursework outside summer disqualifies first-year status. Awards use final cumulative GPA rounded to two decimals; weighted GPA is accepted only when school-wide and with no more than one extra quality point.
notes: State supplements vary; some states receive only the Academic Achievement Award. Preliminary awards are adjusted to the final transcript. Renewal requires a 2.50 GPA, continuous full-time enrollment of at least 12 credits and nonresident tuition status. Full-tuition scholarships exclude these Admissions merit awards.

name: National Scholars Award (NSA)
value: $2,000 to $15,000 per year for up to four years, based on GPA and test scores. No published band table.
deadline: Complete application by February 1, 2027; test scores from tests through December 12, 2026 (self-report or send by February 8, 2027 for more scholarship consideration).
apply: Automatic for nonresident first-year applicants with a complete application by the deadline.
eligibility: Nonresident first-year students entering fall 2027. Test optional: applicants with or without ACT/SAT are considered. Iowa recalculates all GPAs.
notes: Range only; the page gives no GPA or score bands. Merit awards from Admissions do not stack; you get the highest. Renewal: 2.75 UI GPA, full time, nonresident tuition.

name: Non-resident competitive merit scholarships (automatic consideration)
value: Fall 2026 early action non-resident chart (guide only), per year with 3.5 minimum GPA: Academic Presidential 35-36 ACT $17,000, 33-34 ACT $15,000; Academic Heritage 31-32 ACT $11,000; Academic Charter 29-30 ACT $7,000. Previous-year non-resident range $7,000-$17,000 per year.
deadline: For fall 2027: admission application, fee, transcript and official test scores complete by December 1, 2026. Updated scores must arrive by January 11, 2027 for additional scholarship consideration.
apply: Automatic consideration with the admission application; no scholarship application.
eligibility: Nonresident first-year students enrolling in summer or fall immediately after high school. Consideration uses high school GPA and ACT/SAT superscores. The fall 2026 chart requires 3.5 GPA; Auburn recalculates grades if the school does not report on a 4.0 weighted or 100-point scale.
notes: Chart is for fall 2026 and is not a guarantee: each class competes with itself and awards depend on funding. Renewal: 3.0 Auburn GPA and 24 hours per year.

name: Academic Scholar Award for nonresidents
value: Packages of $6,500 to $30,000 per year ($26,000 to $120,000 over four years), including an extra USC Scholarship of at least $500. Last year's averages: $26,000-$30,000 recipients averaged 1450 SAT/33 ACT, 4.7 GPA, top 6%; $16,000-$18,000 averaged 1390/31, 4.5, top 11%; $6,500-$12,000 averaged 1300/28, 4.4, top 14%.

apply: Automatic consideration for all freshmen who apply by December 1.
eligibility: Nonresident first-year applicants. Amounts depend on the applicant pool and funding.
notes: The published statistics are last year's recipient averages, not eligibility minimums or guarantees. Exact amounts depend on the incoming class and funding. Renewal requires full-time enrollment and a 3.0 USC system GPA. Only one general merit award is allowed, except Provost Scholars.

name: Presidential Merit Scholarships
deadline: Priority scholarship date December 1. Merit awards guaranteed to freshmen admitted by April 1 for fall. Upgrade requests by April 1.
apply: Automatic with admission (ApplyTexas or Common App). No additional application.
eligibility: First-time freshmen. Unweighted high school GPA. SAT/ACT superscores used. Test-optional designation is chosen on the application and cannot be changed after the decision. The latest displayed GPA tiers apply to the earlier published cycle; fall 2027 thresholds are not confirmed.
notes: The table covers 2026-2027; fall 2027 amounts are not published. Nonresidents with a Presidential Scholarship qualify for in-state tuition. Renewal requires 30 TTU credits and cumulative GPA 3.5 for $7,000-$9,000 awards, 3.25 for $3,000-$6,500 awards, or 3.0 for $1,000-$2,500 awards; enroll in at least 12 credits each fall and spring.

name: Out-of-State Volunteer Scholarship
value: 2026-27 amounts, per year for four years: 4.0+ UT weighted core GPA and 34-36 ACT or 1490-1600 SAT $18,000 ($72,000); 4.0+ and 30-33 ACT or 1360-1480 SAT $9,000 ($36,000); 3.8+ and 28+ ACT or 1300+ SAT $3,000 ($12,000).

notes: The table is for 2026-2027 and may change for fall 2027. The page gives both December 15 and January 15 admission deadlines. Cannot combine with Orange and White. Renewal requires a 3.0 cumulative GPA, full-time enrollment and satisfactory academic progress.

name: Bluegrass Scholarship (non-residents)
value: Fall 2027, per year, unweighted GPA: test-optional 3.00 $6,500; 3.00 and 25 ACT/1200 SAT (or test-optional 3.50) $10,000; 3.50 and 25 ACT/1200 SAT (or test-optional 3.60) $13,000; 3.50 and 30 ACT/1360 SAT (or test-optional 3.80) $16,000.
deadline: Apply with all documents, including transcript, by December 1, 2026 (Early Action). Accept offers by May 1, 2027.
apply: Automatic for admitted students who meet the criteria and apply by December 1, 2026.
eligibility: Nonresident first-time freshmen entering fall 2027, using unweighted high school GPA and traditional or test-optional criteria. ACT/SAT superscores are not considered. Awards depend on early application and available funds; meeting thresholds does not guarantee an award.
notes: Only one listed UK award is allowed; a competitive or selective scholarship replaces an academic award. Bluegrass is renewable for four years with a 3.0 cumulative GPA and full-time undergraduate enrollment of at least 12 credits each semester.

name: Nonresident merit scholarships (Mark Twain, Border State)
value: Fall 2027 per year for up to four years: Mark Twain Level 1 $21,500; Mark Twain Level 2 $8,500; Border State Award $3,000 (AR, KS, KY, IL, IA, NE, OK, TN; combines with Mark Twain Level 2). Legacy and border-county awards up to $21,500 also listed.

apply: Automatic consideration with a complete admission application by December 1. No separate application.
eligibility: Nonresident first-time freshmen who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents. Awarded on the Mizzou Core GPA and course rigor; test optional (same consideration with or without scores).
notes: No GPA cutoffs are published; merit levels depend on core GPA and rigor. Nonresident awards apply to the nonresident tuition portion and generally do not stack. Border State can combine with Mark Twain Level 2 or Black and Gold Level 2. Renewal requires a 2.75 GPA; online distance programs are ineligible.

name: New Nebraskan Tuition Scholarship
value: New Nebraskan Tuition Scholarship: $20,000 or $15,000 per year toward tuition for up to four years, based on holistic academic review. Full awards assume 15 credits per fall/spring semester and are prorated below 15; summers are excluded.
deadline: For fall 2027: admission priority November 1, 2026 for February 11 scholarship notification; all out-of-state admission materials due May 1, 2027. Supplemental scholarship application for departmental, leadership and service awards is due February 1, 2027.
apply: Automatic consideration with the admission application; supplemental Scholarship Application by February 1 for departmental and leadership awards.
eligibility: Out-of-state first-year students with high academic potential, evaluated holistically using GPA, class rank and optional test scores. Recipients must be U.S. citizens or qualified aliens verified as lawfully present.
notes: The award page does not specify an entering class and says scholarships may change annually. Renewal requires a 3.0 cumulative GPA and 24 completed credits per academic year. Awards apply only to Nebraska-Lincoln tuition.

name: Climb Higher Scholarship (out-of-state)
value: Fall 2027 out-of-state amounts per year: Level 1 3.8+ GPA and ACT 30+ or SAT 1360+ $18,000; Level 2 3.8+ GPA $16,000; Level 3 3.5-3.79 $13,000; Level 4 3.0-3.49 $10,000.

notes: Only Level 1 requires test scores. Renewable for up to eight undergraduate semesters or a first bachelor's degree with 2.75 overall GPA, 30 earned credits per academic year and full-time enrollment. Online programs are ineligible; in-state equivalency arrangements generally exclude nonresident awards.

name: Wildcat Nonresident Award
value: 2027 entry, discount on the nonresident portion of tuition (estimate at 30 hours): 3.90+ 100% (in-state tuition), about $19,101 per year; 3.75-3.89 80%, about $15,281; 3.50-3.74 60%, about $11,461; 3.25-3.49 50%, about $9,551.

apply: Automatic for eligible admitted students. No ACT/SAT needed.

notes: Dollar figures are estimates based on 30 credits. Renewal requires a 3.0 K-State GPA, continuous full-time enrollment and 24 K-State credits per academic year, for up to four years (five for eligible Architecture, Planning and Design programs). This award does not use ACT/SAT scores.

deadline: General freshman timeline lists November 1 early opportunity, February 1 priority, and the Friday before classes start as the final scholarship-materials deadline, without cycle years.

name: Brown and Gold Commitment (non-resident)
value: Published Fall 2026/Spring 2027 Brown and Gold Commitment: $12,000, $8,000, $5,000 or $3,000 annually according to the official GPA/test-score grid. Renewable for up to eight semesters or the first bachelor's degree, whichever comes first.

notes: The award page covers Fall 2026/Spring 2027. The official grid was checked. Funding requires the WyoScholarships general and any applicable recommended applications annually and usually cannot combine with other institutional aid. Renewal requires a 3.0 UW GPA, continuous enrollment in at least 12 credits each fall/spring and 24 completed credits annually.

notes: The page does not identify an entering class. Invitation to Idaho and WUE cannot combine. Renewal requires a 2.5 U of I GPA and continuous full-time enrollment. These are tuition discounts or waivers; the WUE amount is not a separate cash payment.

value: Per year, renewable up to four years, by unweighted GPA: President John R. Park 4.00 $10,000; Provost's 3.90 $8,000; Bonneville 3.80 $6,000; Red Rock 3.70 $4,000; Great Salt Lake 3.50 $3,000.

notes: The official page says fall 2027 scholarship information will be available later this fall. The displayed table applies to 2026-2027. Tuition only, no WUE stacking. Renew with 2.5 GPA, 15 credits per semester and continuous non-resident enrollment until the first degree, for up to four years.

name: Out-of-state freshman academic scholarships
value: 2027 cohort, four-year totals: Cecil C. Humphreys Presidential 3.25+ GPA and 31+ ACT or 1390+ SAT $56,000 ($14,000 per year); Provost 3.25+ and 28-30 or 1300-1380 $48,000 ($12,000); Deans 3.25+ and 24-27 or 1160-1290 $40,000 ($10,000); Academic Achievement 3.25+ and 22-23 or 1100-1150 $28,000 ($7,000); Trustee Award 3.80+ GPA only $20,000 ($5,000).

First-year housing covers standard double occupancy, excluding hall fees and any higher room cost. Renew academic awards with 2.5 USM GPA and 15 credits each semester. GPA is supplied by Admissions from the official transcript; ACT and SAT superscores are accepted.

name: Admission scholarships and Bulldog Out-of-State Scholarship
value: Per year by unweighted GPA (3.0-3.749 / 3.75-4.0): Presidential ACT 33+/SAT 1450-1600 $9,000/$9,500; Deans' ACT 32/1420-1440 $8,000/$8,500; Outstanding Student ACT 31 $6,000/$6,500, 29-30 $5,000/$5,500, 27-28 $4,000/$4,500, 25-26 $3,000/$3,500, 23-24 $2,000/$2,500; Academic Choice ACT 20-22 N/A/$1,000. For the separate Bulldog waiver, admitted students from AR, MS and TX qualify automatically; other-state freshmen need 2.5 unweighted GPA, ACT 23 or SAT 1130 and no remedial English or math requirement. Remedial exemption can be met through the published subscore, GPA, placement-test or college-course options. International students have a separate Bulldog eligibility policy.
notes: The page does not identify an entry year. Merit awards last four years or at most 12 quarters with approved summer use. Maintain continuous enrollment in at least eight credits physically on the main campus and 3.0 cumulative GPA each spring; Presidential scholars need 3.0 each quarter. Bulldog renewal requires at least eight credits per quarter and 2.0 cumulative and quarterly GPA.

name: Out-of-state freshman merit scholarships
deadline: For the 2027-2028 cycle, apply for admission by May 1, 2027. The February ACT or March SAT of senior year is the final score considered.

eligibility: Out-of-state seniors. No superscores. Must be a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, refugee/asylee or otherwise lawfully present.

Current renewal guidance requires 24 UAB credits earned during fall and spring and at least 3.0 cumulative UAB GPA, but final 2027-2028 scholarship policy terms are not yet posted.

name: Rocket Nation Scholarship and automatic merit
value: Fall 2027: renewable merit scholarship of $1,250 to $8,000 per year for 3.0+ GPA, plus Rocket Nation Scholarship of $8,000 per year for out-of-state students with 3.0+ GPA to offset the out-of-state surcharge (about $9,360).

apply: Automatic with admission application; no essays or letters.

Merit and Rocket Nation terms allow up to eight consecutive semesters within five calendar years, ending at the first degree. Full-time attendance, at least 2.0 cumulative GPA, 67% completion of attempted credits each semester and the maximum time frame are required. Rocket Nation reduces the non-resident surcharge and is not refundable; other restricted aid can reduce the award.

name: BG Success Scholarship for out-of-state students
value: BG Success covers half of BGSU's non-resident fee each year and is renewable for four years. BGSU also offers a separate merit scholarship based on a comprehensive admission review.
deadline: Apply for admission by February 18, 2027.
apply: Automatic from the admission application; no extra application.
eligibility: Full-time non-Ohio residents with a 3.0+ cumulative GPA on a 4.0 scale or a 20 ACT or 1040 SAT.
notes: Firelands Pathway students are ineligible. The separate Michigan Out-of-State Scholarship covers the full non-resident fee for residents of Monroe, Lenawee and Wayne counties who meet the same GPA-or-test criteria. General renewal requires full-time enrollment of at least 12 credits, 3.0 cumulative GPA and 30/60/90 completed credits after years one/two/three.

name: Freshman Admission Scholarship (out-of-state)
deadline: Priority deadline for fall 2026 was February 15, 2026.
apply: Automatic review after acceptance as a first-time freshman by the priority date.
eligibility: First-time freshmen outside Alabama who graduated high school no more than four years before admission and have not attended college after graduation. The score-based path requires 3.0+ GPA and ACT superscore 21 or SAT equivalent; U.S. citizens, permanent residents/applicants and students attending U.S. high schools with qualifying visas are eligible. The test-optional path lists U.S. citizens or permanent residents/applicants attending U.S. high schools.
notes: The page publishes fall 2026 awards, with no fall 2027 table. Academic awards and the in-state tuition waiver last up to four years or the first degree. No summer use. Renew with full-time fall/spring enrollment, 30 USA credits per academic year and 3.0 cumulative institutional GPA. Full tuition uses the Arts & Sciences rate for up to 30 credits per year. Awards depend on funding.

name: Academic scholarships and Out-of-State Scholarship
value: 2027-28 per year: A-State Inspire 25+ ACT superscore or 1210 SAT and 3.50 GPA $6,000; A-State Enrichment 21-24 ACT or 1060-1209 SAT and 3.00 $4,000; A-State Endeavor 19-20 ACT or 990-1050 SAT and 3.0 $2,000. Out-of-State Scholarship (24 ACT or 1160 SAT and 3.00 GPA) lowers tuition to the in-state rate and can be combined. Mileage Waiver gives in-state tuition to admitted students from LA, MS, MO, OK, TN, TX.

The out-of-state waivers can combine with an academic award and require full-time attendance; summer waiver use requires full-time attendance in the preceding spring. Student-athletes receiving institutional athletic aid need an individual eligibility determination.

name: Freshman Out-of-State Academic Scholarships
deadline: No separate scholarship application. Scholarship upgrades require updated transcripts and scores received by May 15, 2027.
apply: Automatic for all first-time freshmen offered admission. No separate application.
eligibility: Students who do not live in Alabama or Tennessee; international students living in the U.S. are also eligible. ACT/SAT superscore; ACT Science not used.
notes: Awards cover up to eight fall/spring semesters. Maintain continuous full-time undergraduate enrollment of at least 12 UAH credits each semester, 2.5 cumulative UAH GPA and 24 UAH credits earned across fall and spring. A first spring entrant needs 12 credits and 2.5 GPA by that spring. The official policy allows one year of scholarship probation if renewal criteria are missed.

name: Flagship Scholars Commitment (out-of-state)
value: Fall 2026-Spring 2027: Flagship Match $13,583 to $19,311 per year (matches your home-state flagship cost, eligible states only); Flagship Leaders $9,000 to $12,000 per year; Early Action Award of $3,000-$5,000 extra for early applicants.
deadline: The latest program page gives December 1, 2025 for maximum consideration for fall 2026. The fall 2027 program deadline is not confirmed.
apply: Automatic with admission. No separate application.
eligibility: Out-of-state first-year students with a minimum 2.5 cumulative GPA. Based on GPA and course rigor. Test optional.
notes: The program page and scholarship directory publish 2026-2027 awards, with no fall 2027 award terms. The published awards last at most eight semesters over four years or 120 credits, with satisfactory academic progress, at least six graded credits per semester and the GPA specified in the award letter. Enrolling in fewer than 15 credits can reduce aid. Some commitment funds may be replaced by other grants. FAFSA is encouraged but not required for admission merit awards.

name: Border State Scholarship and Tuition Incentive Program
value: Border State Scholarship lowers tuition to the Kentucky resident rate for first-time freshmen from IL, IN, MO, OH, TN, VA and WV. The separate Tuition Incentive Program Scholarship lowers tuition to the TIP rate for eligible non-residents from other states; the dollar amount varies. Both awards can renew for up to eight full-time semesters or the first degree.
deadline: Complete the admission package, including official admission and high-school transcript, by December 31, 2026.
apply: Automatic from the admission application.
eligibility: Full-time first-time freshmen with at least 12 WKU credits. Border State requires residency in one of the seven eligible states. The separate TIP scholarship requires non-resident status outside those states and receipt of a university scholarship.
notes: Border State and TIP cannot combine with each other or the WKU Family Scholarship. Other eligible university awards can stack up to cost of attendance. These awards do not apply to military, distance-learning or other discounted rates. Renew with at least 2.5 cumulative GPA at the end of spring and full-time enrollment. Awards depend on timely application and available funds.

name: Freshman Guaranteed Scholarships
deadline: For fall 2027, the application, fee or approved waiver, official qualifying ACT/SAT and sixth-semester transcript must be on file, postmarked by December 1, 2026. Accept the award by May 1.
apply: Guaranteed for admitted students who meet all requirements by the priority date. No separate application.
eligibility: First-time freshmen enrolling summer or fall; U.S. citizens or permanent residents. Weighted GPA is accepted when supplied on the official transcript. No superscores. GED and HiSet graduates are ineligible because they do not supply a high-school GPA.
notes: Awards depend on funding and cannot stack with previously awarded guaranteed scholarships. The page describes limited reconsideration for a higher December test score when an official qualifying score was already on file and the student admitted by December 1. Awards last up to eight semesters; maintain full-time fall/spring enrollment throughout each semester in courses applicable to the program and at least 3.0 cumulative GPA. Renewal is checked after every fall and spring.

name: Out-of-state admissions scholarships (Border Benefit, Regional, National)
value: Fall 2027 per year. Border Benefit (IL, IN except 7 counties, MO, OH, TN, VA, WV): in-state tuition (about $16,000) automatic, plus $1,000 (26-27 ACT/1230-1290 SAT), $2,000 (28-29), $3,000 (30), $4,000 (31-35), $5,000 (36) with 3.5 weighted GPA. Regional Scholars (CA, DC Metro, NJ, NY Metro, PA, Southern New England): $12,000 automatic; $13,000 (24-26 ACT and 3.25); $14,000 (27-28 and 3.5); $16,000 (29-36 and 3.5). National Scholars (other states): $5,000 (24+ ACT and 3.0); $7,500 (24+ and 3.25); $10,000 (25-26 and 3.25); $12,000 (27-28 and 3.5); $15,000 (29-36 and 3.5).
deadline: No deadline; guaranteed to students admitted by April 1.
apply: Automatic with admission; no scholarship application.
eligibility: Out-of-state first-time freshmen entering fall 2027. Awards use weighted GPA; qualifying transferable college credit from AP, IB, Cambridge or dual enrollment can replace test scores at specified levels. Border Benefit covers seven states, excluding the seven Southern Indiana counties already charged resident tuition. Regional Scholars covers all counties in CA, DE, NJ, PA, CT, MA and RI, DC, and specified counties in MD, NY and NH; residence or school attendance can qualify. F-1 students have a separate international program.
notes: Admissions scholarships do not stack; receive the highest eligible award. Students in 100% online programs are ineligible. The official page calls these awards renewable but does not publish their duration or detailed renewal requirements; review the award letter. Border Benefit is a tuition-rate reduction, so its approximately $16,000 value can change with tuition.

name: UNT Excellence Scholarship
value: Fall 2026 table, per year by class rank and unweighted GPA (3.75-4.00 / 3.50-3.74 / 3.25-3.49): Top 1% $12,000/$10,000/$8,000; Top 5% $10,000/$8,000/$6,000; Top 10% $8,000/$6,000/$5,000; Top 15% $6,000/$5,000/$4,000; Top 20% $5,000/$4,000/$3,000; Top 25% $4,000/$3,000/$2,000. Bonus $1,000 per year for 1350+ SAT or 30+ ACT. Students who do not qualify are automatically evaluated for a competitive $1,000 UNT Achievement Scholarship.
deadline: For fall 2026: admitted by March 1, 2026 with all transcripts.
apply: Automatic with admission; no separate application.
eligibility: First-time freshmen pursuing a first bachelor's degree and enrolling full-time in the fall immediately after high-school graduation. Excellence uses unweighted GPA and transcript class rank at admission; without a rank, the academic record is reviewed. Applicants without an accredited high-school transcript must provide ACT/SAT for either Excellence or Achievement consideration. International and non-Texas residents can qualify.
notes: The published table applies to fall 2026, with admission and transcripts due March 1, 2026, acceptance May 1, 2026 and bonus test scores July 1, 2026. Awards are competitive and funding limited. Renew up to eight semesters with continuous enrollment in at least 12 UNT credits each fall/spring, 3.0 cumulative UNT GPA and 24 UNT credits earned each academic year. Non-residents may qualify for a competitive tuition waiver subject to Selective Service requirements; it does not waive the out-of-state teaching fee for students living outside Texas.
